_note: Accession registry: the museum's own acquisition history, one row per acquisition lot. `collection` fields on served material (shows, rps) and `sources[].accession` on promotions point here. Two kinds: private-donation (the promoter's own drives and personally-provided documents — the irreplaceable class, arriving as one gift, not one per promotion) and web-recovery (a single bounded public-archive mining campaign, run by this project, with its own dates and its own research digest). Numbered in true acquisition order — no gaps reserved for anybody; a future contributor's lot becomes whatever number is next when their material actually arrives. Accession ids are decimal integers rendered as zero-padded strings ("0001".."9999"); existing ids keep their own padding forever once minted (slug-immutability doctrine, CURATION.md's registry rule), but the padding width is NOT a schema guarantee going forward — once natural growth reaches 10000, new ids simply continue as "10000", "10001", ... with no re-padding and no migration of the ids already minted. Anything that needs to ORDER accession ids must parse them as integers, never compare them as strings/lexically ("9999" < "10000" fails as a string comparison) — this project's own code relies on data/collections.json's own file order (true acquisition order, append-only) rather than re-sorting ids at all, which sidesteps the trap entirely; keep it that way rather than introducing a sort.

What the corpus DOES settle is the cycle before and the cycle beside: the 1997 call for nominations carries the award's own past-winners register, every one of its twenty-seven categories printed with its 1996 winner and its 1997 half-year winner, and the half-year results themselves survive in full with every entrant who drew two or more votes. STRUCTURED: 32 bestowals across 28 award rows — 5 appended to existing RSPWF award rows and 13 new year-end rows, one 1996 winner each; and 10 new half-year rows carrying 14 winners for 1997, four of the twelve half-year categories having ended in a tie. All recipients unminted, on the 2004 precedent. (THE FIRST COMMIT MESSAGE OF THIS LOT SAYS "27 bestowals": that count was wrong — it missed the four tie-doubled half-year bestowals and one appended row. 32 is the count the file carries, and this note is the correction.) awards). Five joins to 2004-named categories deferred rather than asserted, each recorded in the new row's own notes. PRIVACY: 37 markers across the three served documents, 25 distinct terms; every one of them in an out-of-fiction credit — a tabulator's signature, a contact address, and the two sections of the half-year results that name the human beings who ran the federations. 29 rows in this branch's ledger fragment, four of them kept-decisions. FOUR PRE-EXISTING EXPOSURES FLAGGED, NOT FIXED: four of the redacted names already stand in museum-voice frontier notes or another wing's served bio-card. MEMORIAL: the seven clacks names and the Coldblooded Kain / Kain Threat watch, word-bounded and case-insensitive, across all three served documents and every line of new prose — ZERO HITS. Sixteen further 1997 community award series were triaged in the same pass and appended to a workshop file; none of them is served here. The slug is now marked in place on all 3 occurrences (2 in year-end-awards-1997-categories.html, 1 in year-end-awards-1997-call-for-nominations.html); this lot's own PRIVACY count rises to 40 markers across 26 distinct terms in the three served documents. One deny row is filed to this branch's own ledger fragment, widening an existing frontier-scoped deny to cover these two served documents.

The nine Canuck Heat Zone show write-ups of 18 December 2002 to 21 May 2003 are of that kind: they were pulled by Argyle from the Wayback Machine's copies of the federation's own results pages and loaded into the database.
